page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8581C cores with hyper-threading. The instance operates at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture and includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside hardware acceleration flags such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities, with the Geekbench single-core score placing in the top 10% and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression performing in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show relative limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Passmark memory score, and memory bandwidth (both read and write) fall into the bottom 25%. Similarly, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with clang are positioned in the lower 25%, reflecting the constraints of the 4-vCPU allocation on highly parallelized tasks.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4n-highcpu-4 offers a specialized compute-to-memory ratio designed for workloads that prioritize single-threaded execution speed over massive memory capacity or parallel throughput. The inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 instructions provides hardware-level acceleration for specific mathematical and cryptographic operations without requiring GPU resources. This profile is suited for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, text processing, and basic database operations, whereas memory-intensive databases or highly parallel compilation tasks may encounter bottlenecks due to the lower memory bandwidth and limited core count.
